title: Finite filtered additive categories and bounded-below filtered localization
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and use the decreasing filtrations, filtration-preserving maps, finite-filtration predicate and graded quotients of [def-sp-filtration]. The canonical restrictions and graded maps are those of [lem-sp-finite-filtration-induction]; graded complexes have the quotient meaning of [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. For an optional integer interval $B$, let $\mathcal C_B$ be the full subcategory of finite filtered objects, restricted to $F^aX=X$, $F^{b+1}X=0$ when $B=[a,b]$, and unrestricted when no interval is supplied. Let $\mathcal I_B$ be its full subcategory whose graded objects are injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Addition of filtered maps is the underlying addition; these categories have finite products given by finite direct sums with the direct-sum filtration, hence zero objects and finite biproducts. The inclusions, forgetful functor $e_\varnothing$, and graded functors $e_p$ are additive; graded maps are the canonical cokernel maps and preserve identities and composition. Put $K_B^+=K^+(\mathcal C_B)$ and $K_{I,B}^+=K^+(\mathcal I_B)$, using bounded-below integer-indexed complexes modulo chain homotopies valued in the filtered category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with their standard cone triangulations [def-weil-triangulated-category]. No uniform filtration interval is imposed across cochain degrees unless $B$ is supplied. Let $W_B$ be the maps inducing ordinary quasi-isomorphisms on every graded complex. These form a class admitting a left calculus of fractions and compatible with shifts and cone triangles. Define $DF_B^+=K_B^+[W_B^{-1}]$ by formal category localization, with its induced triangulation, $Q_B:K_B^+\to DF_B^+$ its canonical functor, and $c_B:K_{I,B}^+\to DF_B^+$ inclusion followed by $Q_B$, with the induced shift comparison. For any chosen ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], forgetting and grading followed by $K^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal A)$ invert $W_B$. Define $e_p^D:DF_B^+\to D^+(\mathcal A)$ as their canonical localization lifts, including $p=\varnothing$ for forgetting.

proof.text: Identify filtered maps with the subgroup of underlying maps preserving the steps. Uniqueness after the monic step inclusions proves that restriction maps preserve identities, composition and addition. The canonical cokernel projection equations then prove the same laws for graded maps, by epi cancellation. Hence forgetting and every graded functor are additive.

Construct a binary sum with underlying object K plus L and p-th step the subobject represented by the biproduct of the step inclusions. Biprod.map is monic. The biproduct of successive inclusions proves decreasingness. The minimum of lower bounds and maximum of upper bounds give a finite filtration, and fixed bounds are retained. The underlying biproduct projections and inclusions preserve this filtration.

Use the additive graded functor on the category with inj=false. Apply it to the identity pi1;iota1 + pi2;iota2 = id of the constructed binary sum. Given a map into its graded object and a monomorphism, extend its two graded projections using injectivity of the original graded objects. Sum the extended maps followed by the graded inclusions. The displayed identity proves the required factorization, so the sum has injective grades. Construct the zero filtered object explicitly; all its steps and grades are zero. The biproduct identities prove the binary product universal property; terminal plus binary products gives all finite products.

For each integer p pull back the ordinary acyclic triangulated subcategory along the additive graded homotopy functor. Their intersection is closed under isomorphisms and shifts, contains zero, and is closed under the middle term of a distinguished triangle. For any distinguished cone triangle, the ordinary quasi-isomorphism cone criterion shows that its first map is a graded quasi-isomorphism exactly when the cone belongs to this intersection. Thus W is its trW class. Apply Mathlib ObjectProperty.trW.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions and ObjectProperty.trW.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation.

To prove that forgetting sends a graded-acyclic complex to an acyclic complex, fix a degree n and use the three-term filtered complex X^(n-1) -> X^n -> X^(n+1). Every term has a finite filtration; acyclicity of each graded complex is exactness of each graded three-term sequence. Apply finite_filtered_graded_exactness to obtain underlying exactness at n. No uniform bound on filtration across cochain degrees is needed. Transfer this statement to homotopy objects using a quotient representative.

Grading followed by ordinary derived localization inverts W by definition. For forgetting, complete a map in W to a distinguished triangle, whose cone is graded acyclic by the trW characterization. The preceding step makes the underlying cone acyclic. The ordinary cone criterion makes the underlying map a quasi-isomorphism, and ordinary derived localization inverts it. The derived evaluation functors are consequently the canonical localization lifts already defined in the module.
